At sunrise, volunteers gathered beside the old railway station to test a network of low-cost weather sensors. Each device measured rain, wind, temperature, and river height before sending a small report to the city dashboard. Engineers had spent months simplifying the instructions so that neighborhood groups could replace a battery or clean a gauge without special tools. During the first drill, one sensor stopped transmitting, but a librarian found a loose cable and restored it within minutes. The team then compared the local readings with the regional forecast and explained every difference in plain language. Organizers said the experiment was not only about faster warnings. It was also meant to build trust, give residents useful evidence, and make emergency decisions easier to understand.
